rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a large-scale disaster or catastrophe.

example.english: Yesterday’s heavy rain flooded the whole district—it was a real disaster.
example.traditional: 尋日場大雨搞到成區水浸，真係一場災難。
example.jyutping: cam4 jat6 coeng4 daai6 jyu5 gaau2 dou3 seng4 keoi1 seoi2 zam3 zan1 hai6 jat1 coeng4 zoi1 naan6

rows.note: Use 災害 for an official or damage-focused disaster rather than the everyday all-purpose term.

example.traditional: 呢場災害造成多人死亡。
example.jyutping: ni1 coeng4 zoi1 hoi6 zou6 sing4 do1 jan4 sei2 mong4

rows.note: Use 天災 specifically for a natural disaster, not a catastrophe caused by people.

example.english: This typhoon was a natural disaster; there was really no avoiding it.
example.traditional: 今次颱風係天災，真係避無可避。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 toi4 fung1 hai6 tin1 zoi1 zan1 hai6 bei6 mou4 ho2 bei6

rows.note: Use 災禍 for a literary or written description of a calamity rather than ordinary conversation.

example.english: The disaster brought by war still makes the people unable to forget it.
example.traditional: 戰火帶來嘅災禍，至今仍令百姓難以忘懷。
example.jyutping: zin3 fo2 daai3 loi4 ge3 zoi1 wo6 zi3 gam1 jing4 ling6 baak3 sing3 naan4 ji5 mong4 waai4
